Fiiiine... TL;DR: Thank you, Voat. For everything.

 

This is, so far as I can surmise at this time, my final submission on Voat in its final hours. I'd like to take a moment to encapsulate what Voat and its community has meant to me over the last 4 years (as of Dec 8th) of my life. I'll open up with a quick explanation of the sentiment in the title.

 

Nothing lasts, but nothing is lost.

One way or another it was inevitable that my time on Voat would draw to an end or severe tapering. Indeed for the last few months I have been less and less active, seemingly in anticipation of this. In short, I was mentally preparing for an end of sorts. This however has become a highly accelerated process due to the unexpected news of Voat shutting down.

Whatever the case though, the point remains the same. In essence Voat was never going to last for me. But, what Voat has meant to me, what it has taught me and imparted upon me in both a broad sense and a very personal sense, will indeed last a life time; it will not be lost.

 

How did I get here?

To this day, I have only the faintest memory of what started this journey for me; a chance, in the flesh meeting of the most surreal kind with an enigmatic stranger, who asked me to look into pizzagate (or what was rapidly becoming pizzagate) before I'd ever heard of Voat. From there it's a bit of a blur, but I can only surmise that I stumbled across Voat after chancing upon a migration notice on Reddit (simply browsing, I have never had a Reddit account and never will) during my initial scoping out of the situation I had been asked to look into.

It would be some time before I would actually create my account, because when I first arrived – although being vaguely aware of chan culture – this site was a slap to the face in terms of user behavior. I wouldn't say I was shocked, but I had never seen such a broad gathering of (and I don't actually mean offense with this) malcontents and misfits, as well as people dedicated to researching the most extreme and disorienting rabbit holes of what we fondly although sometimes mistakenly call reality. I instinctively decided to "lurk moar" before engaging the crowd over in v/pizzagate.

Eventually I created my account though, and so began the roller coaster ride in earnest.

 

4 years later, what has Voat meant to me?

I'm not even sure where to begin with that...

In the shortest possible sense, I cannot imagine the last 4 years without Voat having been such a strong part of my life. As I look back at the me before and compare with the me of today, I am truly astounded by not only the different states of being I have traversed but how Voat has influenced that progression along the way.

When I first got here I was a very unsure and twisted, heavily drugged (weed mostly) person. Although I had some experience with proverbial rabbit holes, I had felt quite isolated in my spelunking and I was on the arse end of an already transformative time in my life. Getting my bearings and learning to express myself more coherently took a lot of time but I attribute my time on Voat itself to getting me there.

 

Voat has taught me to be more methodical, more focused, more confident than ever. It has taught me to stand up for what I believe in, even in the face of disagreement and hive mentality. It has taught me to be both more trusting but also more discerning. It has taught me to be myself even if that meant being unpopular and/or bursting bubbles and/or not being able to sway others to my point of view.

It has taught me to take criticism and outright lies in stride, and has taught me to be humble (not that these lessons are always applied, but they have certainly been part of the package).

I also learned, incidentally, how much better I can be when I cut weed from my life. Kinda sad, I know, but I can absolutely attribute that lesson in large part to seeing the difference it made on my ability to engage on here.

Voat has had some negative impact too; I won't lie. For a long time it took me away from my family life, my friends; it alienated me. In this last year at least, however, I have come to realize that this was more my fault than Voat's.

Above all, though, Voat gave me a chance to dedicate a good portion of my life to something bigger and more honorable than I can ever hope to be as a single person; the fight against corruption.

 

In the end, I cannot be more thankful for what Voat has brought to my life. For that reason, people such as @Atko, @PuttItOut, @Cynabuns and any others who played a part in constructing and maintaining/administrating the core architecture of Voat will have my lasting gratitude and respect. I sincerely thank you for this opportunity to grow and learn in an environment I came upon seemingly at random (though some may argue it was itself another inevitability).

 

Thank you also, to the following:

The broader Voat community

Friends, foes and all others alike. Those I have fought and researched alongside, and even those who I have fought against and who tried so very hard to censor and ostracize me. Those I have agreed with, those I have disagreed with.

I thank you all for your part in helping me to grow. I thank you all for the community and content you have provided. You're a strange bunch, but, I'm a strange person. Together you have all provided me with an experience I will never ever forget. Although I'll be giving some special mentions ahead, I truly mean it when I say that I appreciate all of you in your own ways; it is after all, our differences and imperfection which makes life interesting, be it here on Voat or elsewhere.
